clue.text: Quietly long to pursue a new sense of style

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so this verb comes after the article and abbreviation

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: Someone quietly yearns for a fresh flair in how they present themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is a flamboyant confidence of manner, a recognisable flair or style.

clue.text: Chasing drug smuggling ring, the French move at a leisurely pace

indicators.note: chasing means running behind, so the French article comes after
smuggling means carrying hidden inside

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
O is ring-shaped
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French police in pursuit of a drug-smuggling gang move slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: To pootle is British slang for to amble or potter about unhurriedly.

clue.text: Two insects head off swimming

indicators.note: taking the head off removes the first letter

parts.note: a gnat and an ant

explanation.surface: A pair of bugs set off for a swim.
explanation.definitionFit: Natant is a formal or zoological adjective for floating or afloat in water.

clue.text: Ruler's graduation perhaps brings age into focus

indicators.note: into means one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: the centre is the focal point
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A monarch's university graduation makes everyone notice how old they are.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruler is a measuring stick, not a monarch; its markings are graduations.
explanation.definitionFit: A centimetre is one of the marked divisions along a measuring stick, an example of a graduation.

clue.text: Note the empty, regressive system of values

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the combination is reversed

parts.note: soh is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: emptying a word leaves only its outside letters

parts.note: the word the with its middle letter emptied out leaves its two ends

explanation.surface: A note about a hollow, backward-looking set of principles.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the guiding beliefs or moral character of a group or culture.

clue.text: International appearance by Bale, in trouble with qualification, …

parts.note: a player winning a cap has appeared for their national team

indicators.note: being in trouble suggests a mess, so the footballer's name is jumbled

explanation.surface: Gareth Bale's international appearance has a fitness question hanging over it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs into the next clue for the surface only; the wordplay is complete here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone capable is competent, having the qualification or ability needed for a task.

clue.text: Winner is a cheat, getting nothing right under detailed questioning

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means placed below the earlier parts

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick

indicators.note: detailed means de-tailed, losing its last letter

parts.note: a query is a question
O is zero

explanation.surface: A victor is exposed as a cheat but gets nowhere under close interrogation.
explanation.walkthrough: Detailed is read as de-tailed, docking the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A conqueror is one who defeats others, a victor.

clue.text: Agreement is in the bag we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals a word heard, not seen

parts.note: something in the bag has been packed

explanation.surface: A deal is sealed, or so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: In the bag also suggests a done deal, which helps the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal deal or treaty between parties.

clue.text: City institute faces rising trouble with leading supporters

indicators.note: leading puts these at the front

parts.note: bras are supporting garments

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A city's institute faces mounting difficulties, with its main backers in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Brasilia is the capital of Brazil, a planned modernist metropolis.

clue.text: Attractive and authentic, in gingham trousers?

indicators.note: as a verb, to trouser is to pocket, so the words keep the answer inside them

parts.note: the run of letters straddles the end of authentic, the word in and the start of gingham

explanation.surface: Genuine gingham trousers are an appealing look.
explanation.walkthrough: Trousers looks like clothing but is a verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Enticing means tempting or alluring, drawing someone in.

clue.text: … time and again losing head from temper

indicators.note: losing its head means the verb drops its first letter

parts.note: to temper something is to soften or moderate it

explanation.surface: Continuing the footballer's tale: repeatedly losing his cool in a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means frequently, happening repeatedly over and over.

clue.text: Manually produce floating structure after a couple of taps?

indicators.note: after means this structure follows the pair of taps

parts.note: basin taps are marked H and C, hot and cold
a raft is a simple floating platform

explanation.surface: Building a raft by hand, perhaps after tapping a couple of times.
explanation.walkthrough: H and C, for hot and cold, is the standard pair of taps on a basin.
explanation.definitionFit: To handcraft something is to make it with skilled hands rather than by machine.

clue.text: O'Neill's put pickled item on the menu?

indicators.note: something pickled is preserved, but also drunk and muddled, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A pub called O'Neill's has added a pickled snack to its menu.
explanation.definitionFit: This pulse-based soup is a common dish listed by restaurants and cafes.

clue.text: A little sleep at home then cocaine? This could have a galvanising effect!

definitions.text: This could have a galvanising effect!

parts.note: a single z stands for sleep, as in cartoon snoring
someone in is at home
C is the street and chemistry shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A quick nap at home, then a line of cocaine, would certainly energise you.
explanation.walkthrough: Galvanising here is literal: steel is galvanised by coating it with this metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Galvanising means coating iron or steel with this metal to protect it from rust.

clue.text: Possible cause of downfall of crazy family

parts.note: bananas is slang for mad
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A mad family could bring about someone's ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipping on a discarded peel is the comic-strip way of taking a tumble.

clue.text: Flower displayed by people supporting F1 Ferrari?

parts.note: Ferrari's Formula One cars are famously red
a team's fans are often styled its nation, the whole people behind it

explanation.surface: Fans of the Ferrari Formula One team wear a particular bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as RED CAR plus NATION, the Ferrari fan base.
explanation.definitionFit: The carnation is a garden bloom, and the red variety is a common buttonhole.

clue.text: Instruments from Spain turned up in Paris, ten at Sacré-Cœur?

indicators.note: turned up in a down answer means read from bottom to top, so backwards
in says the letters lie inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run from the last of Paris through ten and at to the start of Sacré-Cœur

explanation.surface: Spanish musical instruments appeared at the Paris basilica, ten of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Castanets are clicking hand-held percussion pieces associated with flamenco dancing.

clue.text: Prepares for the theatre with wine bottles emptied during drink

indicators.note: during means placed inside the drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a cru is a French wine of a given vineyard

indicators.note: emptied leaves only the outer letters

parts.note: the word bottles with its inside removed keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An actor gets ready for the show with emptied wine bottles mid-drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Theatre here is the operating theatre, where surgeons wash before operating.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon scrubs up, washing hands and arms thoroughly before an operation.

clue.text: Trainee heads east, close to perfect place for surfing?

indicators.note: heads means goes first, so the trainee precedes the compass point

parts.note: an intern is a trainee

indicators.note: close to means the last letter

parts.note: the final letter of perfect is the one taken

explanation.surface: A trainee travels east, near the perfect spot for catching waves.
explanation.walkthrough: Surfing refers to browsing websites, not riding waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Surfing the web means browsing online pages, so the online network is where it happens.

clue.text: Expansion following recent cycling feature in middle of the paper

definitions.text: feature in middle of the paper

indicators.note: following puts this word after the jumbled one
cycling means the letters go round and are rearranged

parts.note: spread is growth or extension over a wider area

explanation.surface: A newspaper's middle pages carry a recent feature on growing interest in cycling.
explanation.definitionFit: A centrespread is the pair of facing pages at the centre of a magazine or newspaper.

clue.text: Promise of partnership after politician displays desire

indicators.note: after means the vow comes behind the politician

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal
I do is the marriage vow

explanation.surface: A politician's wedding vow reveals their passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual drive or appetite.

clue.text: Missing Columbia's capital, cyclone devastated the old country

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so the rest is rearranged
missing means a letter is taken out
a capital is the first letter

parts.note: the capital, or opening letter, of Columbia is the one dropped

explanation.surface: A storm missed the capital of Columbia but devastated an old nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceylon was the former name of Sri Lanka, hence an old country.

clue.text: Unsteady, regularly absent and had taken drugs

indicators.note: letters missing at regular intervals leaves every other one

parts.note: taking the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of unsteady spells the answer

explanation.surface: Someone wobbly, often missing, who had been on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Used is a slang verb for taking illegal drugs, so the past form fits.

clue.text: Reordered arsenic bottles, tea and sweetener

indicators.note: to bottle is to contain, so the jumble holds the drink inside
reordered tells us to rearrange the poison's letters

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea

explanation.surface: A poisoner rearranges arsenic bottles alongside the tea and sugar substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Saccharine is an artificial sugar substitute used in food and drink.

clue.text: Unblocked net

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to make as profit after deductions

explanation.walkthrough: Net looks like a noun, but it is the verb to earn after costs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for free of obstruction and a verb for earning as profit.

clue.text: Picked up instruction for starters and ingredient for pudding

indicators.note: picked up means heard, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: a race starter may tell runners to go, so say go

explanation.surface: Someone notes cooking instructions for the first course and an ingredient for dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: Starters are race starters, not first courses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch from palm pith used to make a milk dessert.

clue.text: Senile and has confused language

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone elderly and muddled has lost their grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinhalese is the main tongue spoken in Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Alaskan ice traps river crustaceans

indicators.note: trapping something holds it inside, so the river letter goes within

parts.note: ice is American slang for murder, so an American, here Alaskan, ice is to kill

explanation.surface: Arctic sea ice holds tiny shellfish in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Krill are tiny shrimp-like marine animals eaten by whales.

clue.text: Regulars annually knocked back quick drink

parts.note: PA is per annum, yearly

indicators.note: knocked back means the drink is read backwards, as well as swallowed

parts.note: a snort is a quick shot of spirits

explanation.surface: Pub regulars knock back a quick drink every year.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrons are a shop's or pub's regular customers.

clue.text: In poor shape in Germany and with badly worn clothing

indicators.note: clothing a thing means wrapping round it, so the jumbled word goes outside
badly means the letters are put in disorder

parts.note: und is the German word for and

explanation.surface: Someone in poor condition in Germany, wearing shabby clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Run-down means tired, neglected or in poor condition.
